properties.name: Forging of the Sampo
properties.summary: The eternal sage Väinämöinen commissioned the smith Ilmarinen to forge the Sampo, a magical artifact that produced flour, salt, and gold. It was given to Louhi, mistress of Pohjola (the North), as a bride-price. When Väinämöinen, Ilmarinen, and Lemminkäinen attempted to steal it back, the Sampo was shattered in a sea battle.

properties.name: Väinämöinen's Creation Song
properties.summary: The goddess Ilmatar lay floating on the primordial ocean. A teal laid seven eggs on her knee; they broke and formed the earth, sky, sun, and moon. From the waters Väinämöinen was born, an ancient sage who sang the world into being. His songs had the power to reshape reality itself.

properties.name: Väinämöinen's Journey to Tuonela
properties.summary: Väinämöinen journeyed to Tuonela, the Finnish underworld, seeking magical knowledge. He crossed the dark river and was received by the death goddess Tuonetar, who offered him beer of forgetfulness. Iron nets were cast to trap him. Using his shape-shifting powers, Väinämöinen escaped as a snake, warning others never to visit Tuonela voluntarily.

properties.name: Lemminkäinen's Death and Resurrection
properties.summary: The reckless hero Lemminkäinen was killed trying to shoot the swan of Tuonela. His body was hacked to pieces and thrown into the river of the dead. His mother, sensing his death, raked the river with a copper rake, gathered every fragment, and sang him back to life — the power of a mother's love and magic defeating death.
